change_control: Record rationale and old/new policy hashes before rerunning affected selection measurements.
sequence: H(G) versus the same G measurements
initial_workload_weights: Equal weights across the eight workloads; census-driven revisions must be frozen and hashed before selection measurements.
run_order: Seeded randomized paired candidate/baseline trials on the same dedicated host and engine tier.
estimator: Geometric mean of paired runtime ratios across the fixed workload weights; paired bootstrap over independent trials, not inner iterations, with seed and 10000 resamples recorded.
uniform_rule: Choose the simplest candidate whose upper 95% confidence bound for runtime ratio to the measured best is at most 1.05. If uncertainty exceeds the bound, gather more trials or record no selection.
hybrid_rule: Select H only when the lower 95% confidence bound on representative speedup versus its own G is at least 10%, and upper bounds on each regression/resource ratio meet all budgets. Include incremental checks, adapters, stubs, frame/root costs and table storage. H failing selection does not mean its evidence can be omitted.
engine_policy: Pin engine/version/tier, host CPU/OS, flags and toolchain. Qualify multivalue, tail calls, selected EH encoding, shared-memory atomics and bulk memory explicitly. JSPI is required only for its profile. No cross-engine pooling.

dedicated_host_progress_limits.scope: Controlled harness on the recorded dedicated host; these limits do not promise browser background-tab or OS scheduling latency. A timeout fails the run and is investigated, never counted as success.

ratio_definitions: runtime_ratio = candidate runtime / baseline runtime; speedup = (1 / runtime_ratio) - 1. Resource growth = candidate / baseline - 1.
